evidence.snippet: As in PV patients, early lesions showed suprabasilar acantholysis with later lesions showing inflammatory erosions.

nodes.description: Biallelic DSG3 variants remove desmoglein 3 from the desmosomes of stratified squamous epithelia. Reported alleles are a homozygous nonsense variant, a homozygous 49.6 kb deletion at 18q12.1 that removes the last exon of DSG3 and also involves DSG2, and a homozygous missense variant. This is the structural-gene route of the desmosomal adhesion failure module: the protein that IgG autoantibodies block in pemphigus vulgaris is here genetically absent.

evidence.reference_title: Homozygous deletion of the DSG3 terminal exon associated with acantholytic blistering of the oral and laryngeal mucosa.
evidence.snippet: We report a novel homozygous 49.6 kb deletion of chromosome 18q12.1 involving the last exon of DSG3 in dizygotic twins with phenotype consistent with acantholytic blistering of the oral and laryngeal mucosa (ABOLM).

evidence.reference_title: Homozygous deletion of the DSG3 terminal exon associated with acantholytic blistering of the oral and laryngeal mucosa.
evidence.snippet: Functional studies would further clarify how deletions resulting in loss of function of DSG3 may cause the reported phenotypes of DSG3-related ABOLM.

evidence.reference_title: Targeted disruption of the pemphigus vulgaris antigen (desmoglein 3) gene in mice causes loss of keratinocyte cell adhesion with a phenotype similar to pemphigus vulgaris.
evidence.snippet: DSG3 -/- mice had no DSG3 mRNA by RNase protection assay and no Dsg3 protein by immunofluorescence (IF) and immunoblots.

evidence.reference_title: Explanations for the clinical and microscopic localization of lesions in pemphigus foliaceus and vulgaris.
evidence.snippet: These studies suggest that pemphigus autoantibodies inhibit the adhesive function of desmoglein proteins, and demonstrate that either Dsg1 or Dsg3 alone is sufficient to maintain keratinocyte adhesion.

nodes.description: Targeted disruption of Dsg3 produces oral mucosal erosions with suprabasal acantholysis, runting from impaired feeding, and telogen hair loss. The balding (bal) mutant is allelic.
Ruptured oral blisters leave erosions of the oral mucosa.

evidence.snippet: The deletion also involved the DSG2 gene, which is associated with arrhythmogenic right ventricular dysplasia (ARVD). The affected siblings and heterozygous parents do not show any cardiac phenotype at this time.

nodes.description: Desmoglein 1 can substitute for desmoglein 3 where it is expressed at sufficient levels. In epidermis it is abundant, but in oral and other squamous mucosa it is expressed at much lower levels than desmoglein 3. The lack of compensation explains why loss of desmoglein 3 presents as a mucosal rather than a cutaneous disease. This node is inferred from pemphigus and mouse genetic studies; desmoglein 1 expression has not been measured in ABOLM patient tissue.
nodes.id: Insufficient Desmoglein 1 Compensation in Squamous Mucosa

evidence.reference_title: Lack of mucosal involvement in pemphigus foliaceus may be due to low expression of desmoglein 1.
evidence.snippet: In the mucosal extract, the Dsg1 band was much weaker than Dsg3, whereas in the epidermal extract the Dsg1 band was stronger than Dsg3.

evidence.reference_title: Expression of desmoglein 1 compensates for genetic loss of desmoglein 3 in keratinocyte adhesion.
evidence.snippet: These studies show that desmoglein-1 can compensate for loss of desmoglein-3-mediated adhesion, and provide genetic evidence confirming the desmoglein compensation hypothesis.
